prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Tobias Reyne for the job below.

About the freelancer: 7 years experience; skills: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack, HTML and CSS

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Make amendments to Shopify store
I will send all references upon request. - change logo to emblem in header when scrolling down (SEE REFERENCE 1) - Add ticker promotion banner to the top of page (See reference 2) - Make header and banner sticky - Change currency converter as current one is not working - Error with the product page when scroll to the right (see reference 3) - show price below the image on home page (see reference 4) - Image on home page with border and button in the middle with box (see reference 5)
</job>

Past projects you may mention (the ONLY experience you may claim):
title: Home goods storefront rebuild
client: Juniper & Ash Home
client_industry: e-commerce
start: 2021-01
end: 2021-04
engagement: fixed
stack:
- Next.js
- Tailwind CSS
- Stripe
- Sanity
- Vercel
built: Replaced a slow theme-based shop with a headless storefront and CMS the marketing
  team edits themselves.
metrics:
- largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.3s
- organic traffic +38% in 3 months

Style:
- Open by restating the client's specific problem in one sentence.
- Mention these projects by what was built and one result each: Home goods storefront rebuild (p03).
- Keep it under 150 words.
- End with one specific question about the job.

Output only the proposal text. Never add contact details or links.
text:
You need a set of Shopify UI and header fixes: scrolling logo swap, sticky promo banner and header, currency converter repair, product page scroll issue, and homepage image/price layout updates.

I’m Tobias Reyne, a full-stack developer with 7 years of experience working with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. I can handle the front-end behavior and layout adjustments you listed, and I’m comfortable working from reference examples to match the intended design.

One relevant project I built was a home goods storefront rebuild for Juniper & Ash Home, where I replaced a slow theme-based shop with a headless storefront and CMS the marketing team could edit themselves. That work reduced largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.3s and increased organic traffic by 38% in 3 months.

Do you want the header/logo swap and ticker banner implemented using the current theme structure, or are you open to a custom section/script approach if needed?
